Article Title: Gyanesh Kumar should be criminally prosecuted for 'treason': Priyanka Gandhi on SIR row
Article Text:
Cong MP Priyanka Gandhi targets EC over SIR, alleges 'voter roll tampering'.

'Electoral process completely tainted': Cong

'All actions have been in accordance': EC

'All three Commissioners were unanimous': BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday slammed the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that he should be "criminally prosecuted" if found responsible for "tampering with electoral rolls and deleting voters' names. "Her remarks came a day after The Indian Express published a report claiming that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Speaking to reporters in Wayanad, Kerala, Priyanka Gandhi said, "Anybody who plays around with the process, the democratic process of our elections is committing treason against this nation. That is our very clear stand. I do not think anybody in that position should have legal protection in the way that he has. The Chief Election Commissioner has. If they have done illegal acts because tampering with the voters' rolls, deleting, I believe, 13 crore voters is a criminal act against democracy, against the Constitution and against the nation. ""Since criminal acts fall under a particular law, and people are usually tried and prosecuted for doing those criminal acts, I do not see why the Election Commissioner has to have any protection against it," the Congress MP said."If he has done an illegal act, he has been fully aware that this is happening under his nose. His colleagues have brought it to his attention. He has ignored it and intentionally allowed an unfair election to take place. He should be criminally prosecuted just like any other criminal, and he should be tried for treason. This is my very clear stand," she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Priyanka Gandhi had also called the issue "an extremely serious" one for democracy."This is an extremely serious issue for our democracy. If there are no elections, then where is democracy? If elections are unfair and rigged in any manner, then the Election Commission is assisting in that. If the Election Commissioner is not only aware of it but also allowing it to happen, then it is a very serious assault on democracy. It is an act of treason," she said.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also launched a fresh attack on Gyanesh Kumar , alleging irregularities in the ECINet software and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Ramesh said a series of reports had raised serious questions over the functioning of the poll panel and alleged that the electoral process had been "completely compromised and tainted".He said, "Yesterday, sensational revelations in a major national daily brought to light that the CEC has completely undermined the integrity, reliability, and competence of the Election Commission. This morning, another report in this series has emerged."Ramesh alleged that Goa's chief electoral officer (CEO) wrote to the ECI eight times in seven days seeking the reinstatement of valid voters whose names had been removed by the ECINet software. He said Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) had confirmed that the voters were valid, but their emails were ignored and the names were removed.He also stated that the process for adding new voters through Form 6 had been made more difficult and claimed that Gen Z was being "deliberately targeted" to exclude young voters from electoral rolls.Ramesh said the latest allegations reinforced what leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi had been saying for nearly two years, referring to the results of the Haryana and Maharashtra assembly elections."The electoral process has been completely compromised and tainted. This is the implementation of the Method of Disenfranchising Indians (MODI) by Gyanesh Kumar," Ramesh said.He also called for the CEC's resignation, saying, "If there is even a shred of decency and ethics left in CEC Gyanesh Kumar, his first step should be to immediately resign from his position. After that, the Prime Minister and Home Minister will be held accountable for their nefarious designs."Earlier on Wednesday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi described "vote chori" as a "crime against the Indian people" and an attack on the Constitution.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served."In a video, he also addressed the Election Commission and election officials, saying, "I am clearly telling the Election Commission and election officers: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason; it is against the nation. Do not forget this. The time will come! We will catch you! You will not be spared."According to the media report, Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had objected at least 14 times to decisions taken in the Commission's name without their knowledge or approval. The reported objections covered issues including voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 and the handling of the electoral-roll database.The ECI rejected the suggestion that the reported objections amounted to a division within the Commission. ECI officials said all decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of all three commissioners.In a statement, the poll panel said, "The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour. All actions of ECI have been in accordance with laws and instructions of the Commission. All official orders, decisions and administrative directions issued by the Commission carry full legal sanctions and follow established statutory procedures."The Commission further said, "Any operational queries or inputs raised by Commission members during draft stages are part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights. The suggestions given by the Commissioners were for further improving the electoral processes," adding that differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations.BJP national spokesperson and MP Sambit Patra earlier defended the functioning of the Election Commission, saying discussions among the three commissioners were part of the democratic process."Look at the situation: if the three Election Commissioners do not communicate with each other, if there is no exchange of views or consultation, and they simply agree to everything, then the opposition parties claim it is a dictatorship. They say this government appointed these three commissioners; they just say yes. Now, there have been 14 instances of correspondence among the three of them, official deliberations, as far as we gather from the media. It is not as if the Bharatiya Janata Party goes and reads these letters; rather, reports in the media indicate that official deliberations took place among the three, which is a sign of a healthy democracy," he said."I would say that today, all the opposition parties have fallen into a trap, the trap of claiming that the Election Commission and the government were acting dictatorially. On the contrary, I would say this is pure democracy.Deliberations are taking place, and the Election Commission has stated very clearly in the very first paragraph of its document that, following all official democratic deliberations, the final outcome, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), was achieved with unanimity," Patra said."In other words, all three Commissioners were unanimous; there was no difference of opinion or dissent among them," he added.Meanwhile, ECI sources maintained that all decisions taken by the poll panel, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of both Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: Cong mp priyanka gandhi targets ec over sir, alleges 'voter roll tampering' 'electoral process completely tainted': cong. 'all actions have been in accordance': ec. Congress leader rahul gandhi described "vote chori" as a "crime against the indian people" and an attack on the constitution.

Article Title: 'In front row of crises, back row of policy making': Jaishankar pushes for stronger Global South
Article Text:
Jaishankar said energy security is at the heart of development, and availability and prices should not be manipulated for political ends.

Chairing a high-level meeting of Global South countries on the sidelines of UNGA, external affairs minister S Jaishankar stressed the need to work towards food and energy security, fair economic and trade practices, while rejecting supply chain and connectivity choke points.Stressing the importance of pending global governance reforms, he said the world was witnessing dismantling of multilateralism at a time when developing countries were turning towards it."Now the fact is also that institutions created for a different era continue to reflect the power structures of that era, and Global South today may be in the front row of global crises, but is in the back row of decision-making," said Jaishankar, adding for Global South there has never been a moment as critical as right now for solidarity.He said energy security is at the heart of development, and availability and prices should not be manipulated for political ends. The EAM was addressing a high-level meeting of like-minded Global South nations and friends under the theme of 'Navigating Together Towards a Brighter Future - the Compelling Case for an Empowered Global South'.The participants discussed the challenges Global South countries are facing, including ongoing conflicts' impact on energy security, volatility in trade and investment flows, concerns of seafarers in ongoing conflicts.They also expressed concern over the weakening of multilateral institutions while emphasising the urgent need for comprehensive UN reforms.Jaishankar underlined the need to ensure fair economic and trade practices that can enhance developing countries' production capabilities. "Our right to industrialise must not be denied," he said.He also raised the issue of safety of seafarers, saying the maritime commons must be secured, international law observed, and safety and security of seafarers and commercial shipping guaranteed.Jaishankar underlined that the transformation being brought about by AI must not create new divides. "We could share indigenously developed tools and frameworks for the benefit of Global South members, and ensure that AI remains human-centric," he said.He also suggested closer economic cooperation among Global South as a necessary buffer against the fallout of overlapping global crises.
Article Summary: Jaishankar said energy security is at the heart of development, and availability and prices should not be manipulated for political ends. The eam was addressing a high-level meeting of like-minded global south nations and friends under the theme of 'navigating together towards a brighter future'

NEW DELHI: Germany's relationship with India has assumed greater importance amid growing global uncertainty, with the two countries looking to deepen cooperation in trade, defence and labour mobility, German ambassador to India, Jasper Wieck, said at a press conference Wednesday.He said Germany was ready to sign an $8 billion deal with India for building six next-generation conventional submarines. "In terms of documents, it has already been finalised and the German side has agreed to it. It is now up to the Indian side to complete and conclude its internal processes," Wieck said, adding Germany was ready to sign the agreement as early as tomorrow.The agreement will see TKMS, the German defence contractor that will supply advanced submarine design and technology transfer, partnering with India's MDL.Describing the current global situation as an "era of unpredictability", Wieck said Russia had "wrecked trust and peace" while US was "constantly changing the rules of the game", making closer cooperation between India and Germany more important.Wieck assumed charge as Germany's ambassador to India and Bhutan recently.Asked about his three priorities as ambassador, Wieck identified the pending formal signing of the India-European Union FTA, labour migration, and defence cooperation.On India's continued purchase of Russian oil, he said Germany understood the energy needs of a country of 1.4 billion people but argued that reducing purchases of Russian oil would dent Moscow's ability to finance the war in Ukraine. "If we don't buy any oil anymore from Russia then financing for the (Ukraine) war stops," he said.On pending student visa issues, he said Germany was working to address the issue.

Article Title: 1 Indian killed, 19 rescued after MV Cape Dao attacked off Oman; MEA calls for end to shipping attacks
Article Text:
(Representative image): The MEA said its embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the rescued Indian seafarers.

India condemns attack

Embassy coordinating with Oman

Government orders repatriation

An Indian seafarer, identified as Wiper Suraj Yadav from Uttar Pradesh, was killed after a missile attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier MV Cape Dao off the east coast of Oman, while all 19 other Indian crew members were safely evacuated, the government said on Wednesday.Yadav succumbed to head injuries sustained in the attack, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said. The vessel had 20 Indian seafarers on board, with the surviving crew evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and brought ashore.Sonowal said directions had been issued to maritime authorities to coordinate with Omani authorities and the ship management company for the immediate and safe repatriation of the surviving Indian crew.“The government will ensure that the mortal remains of Suraj Yadav are brought home with full dignity, and every possible support is extended to his next of kin,” Sonowal said.The ministry of external affairs condemned the attack and said continuing incidents targeting commercial shipping in the region were “deeply worrisome”.“Of the 20 Indian seafarers on board, 19 have been rescued, while 1 Indian national tragically lost his life.We offer our deepest condolences to the family of the deceased,” the MEA said.The ministry said its embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the Indian seafarers. It also thanked the Omani authorities for their support.“We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MV Cape Dao earlier today off the east coast of Oman,” the MEA said.It called for an end to attacks targeting commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region. India also reiterated its call for free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways.“The continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. We reiterate our call for dialogue and diplomacy to de-escalate tensions and enable early return of peace to the region,” the MEA said.The Indian embassy in Oman said it was in close coordination with Omani authorities over the safety of the crew and was monitoring the situation.“We are closely monitoring the attack on MV Cape Dao today while transiting toward India, and are in close coordination with Omani authorities regarding the safety of all crew on board, including 19 Indian nationals,” the embassy said in a post on X.The mission also expressed condolences to the family of the Indian seafarer who was killed.“We are deeply saddened by the loss of one Indian national in this attack. Our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. The Mission is coordinating with the RPSL and is in touch with the family of the deceased,” it added.The MEA said the embassy was proactively coordinating with the Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the Indian seafarers.Sonowal said maritime authorities had been directed to work closely with Omani authorities and the ship management company to ensure the surviving crew members return home safely.He also offered condolences to Yadav’s family and said the government would provide all possible support to his next of kin.India has consistently called for safe and free navigation in international waters and the unhindered flow of commerce through international waterways.
Article Summary: An indian seafarer, identified as wiper suraj yadav from uttar pradesh, was killed after a missile attack on the antigua and barbuda-flagged bulk carrier mv cape dao off the east coast of oman. The vessel had 20 indian seafarers on board, with the surviving crew evacuated by the royal navy of oman and brought ashore.

Article Title: India's proposal under consideration for safe Black Sea shipping, Zelenskyy says
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Picture credit: PTI)

India has been pushing for dialogue

Black Sea shipping remains key concern

Russia yet to back proposals

India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying Egypt, India and Turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine.Speaking to leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to support a maritime truce based on the proposals and that Russia now needed to respond.“We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere,” Zelenskyy said.The remarks came at Ukraine's Crimean Platform summit on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine.The reference to India's role comes amid New Delhi's efforts to remain engaged with both Moscow and Kyiv and encourage an end to the conflict.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said earlier this month that India had been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and was exploring ideas that could contribute to mitigating and eventually ending the war.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” Jaishankar said during his visit to Warsaw.Jaishankar has also said India's position is that the conflict should end through dialogue and diplomacy.During his visit to Kyiv earlier this month, he met Zelenskyy and Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, with discussions including possible approaches to ending the conflict.“If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there,” Jaishankar said in Kyiv.According to Reuters, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Turkey had proposed options to restore safe navigation for merchant vessels in the Black Sea, where cargo movements have been severely disrupted by attacks on ships and port infrastructure by both sides.Ukraine has been seeking ceasefires covering attacks on energy infrastructure as well as shipping in the Black Sea. Kyiv has also expressed concern that Russia could target power and heating facilities with missiles and drones during the winter.The disruption has also affected countries dependent on grain supplies from the Black Sea region. Reuters reported that wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa have faced difficulties securing supplies, while global wheat prices have risen.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to ensure safe shipping and food security if Russia was prepared to take steps towards de-escalation.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov on Wednesday that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy.The Kremlin has not publicly backed the proposals.Ahead of the Rubio-Lavrov meeting, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there were currently no grounds for broader peace talks, while maintaining that Russia remained open to negotiations.“For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks,” Peskov said.Zelenskyy also said he was ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump.The latest developments come as India continues its diplomatic engagement with both sides.Jaishankar met US secretary of state Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Wednesday and discussed the Ukraine situation, as well as India's concerns over the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.
Article Summary: India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the black sea. Ukraine's president volodymyr zelenskyy said egypt, india and turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between russia and ukraine.

Article Title: 'Judiciary plays second fiddle to govt in judges' appointment’: SC Justice Datta defends collegium system
Article Text:
SC judge on collegium system

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Describing the argument that “judges appoint judges” as a "myth," Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Dutta said on Wednesday that the judiciary, in fact, plays “second fiddle” to the government in the appointment of judges.“This court is left to wonder why, even after the judiciary has been relegated to playing second fiddle to the executive in the matter of appointment of judges, is there still a clamour to induct an outsider at the stage of selection,” PTI quoted Justice Dipankar Datta as saying. According to the judge, the argument, coming from the executive, was a “feeble attempt to deflect attention from its own dereliction and failure”, rejecting the government’s argument that drew a parallel between the absence of an “outsider” in the collegium system of judicial appointments and the CJI's removal from the three-member Election Commission appointment panel headed by the prime minister.To underscore his “second fiddle” argument, Justice Dipankar Datta pointed to the government’s “selective” implementation of collegium resolutions, saying this undermines their sanctity. While acknowledging that the government approves a majority of the names recommended by the collegium, he noted that at least one is invariably withheld.“The sanctity of a collegium resolution is lost each time the executive implements it selectively, albeit approving the majority of those recommended while withholding at least one.Undeterred by such peaceful approvals and regardless of the fate of those not cleared by the executive, the collegium chooses to proceed seemingly to avoid a head-on conflict with the executive, and is left with the option to keep the institution running. The collegium thereby avoids a constitutional crisis,” Justice Datta said.On the “sweeping generalisation” that the collegium acts as a “law unto itself,” Justice Datta pointed to the detailed consultative process involved in judicial appointments, including the roles played by the central and state governments, intelligence agencies and other bodies in vetting credentials.He also noted that every appointment involves the formal — and final — approval of the President of India.“It has become fashionable nowadays to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations are exceptions and not the norm, and that no system can guarantee infallibility of human choice. The uninitiated and the unversed unknowingly have thus been made to believe that the collegium of the Supreme Court and the collegium of the high courts comprise judges, who appoint judges,” Justice Datta stated.“Despite all its opacity and imperfections, the collegium system still remains the most viable option for safeguarding independence, as envisioned under Article 50 of the Constitution by its framers,” he added.Justice Datta made the observations in a split verdict delivered by a bench that also comprised Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.The bench was hearing a batch of petitions challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel responsible for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
Article Summary: Supreme court justice dipankar dutta says the judiciary plays "second fiddle" to the government in the appointment of judges. According to the judge, the argument, coming from the executive, was a “feeble attempt to deflect attention from its own dereliction and failure”

Article Title: Israeli soldier accused of Gaza war crimes leaves India after complaint by Palestinian group: Report
Article Text:
The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid-September.

Second Israeli soldier to leave India after complaint

An Israeli soldier accused of alleged war crimes in Gaza has left India weeks after the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF), a Palestinian rights group, filed a criminal complaint against him, according to a report by Middle East Eye.The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid-September, a lawyer familiar with the case told Middle East Eye. It remains unclear whether the complaint influenced his departure or whether he left after completing his holiday.The development comes amid renewed calls for countries to uphold international law. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, speaking on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Monday, said multilateralism works best when international law, rules and norms are "scrupulously observed".The latest case marks the second incident this year in which the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has identified an Israeli soldier travelling in India and filed a complaint against him.In June, the Brussels-based organisation approached Indian authorities seeking the arrest of Eitan Gilboa, an Israeli military reservist who was vacationing in Himachal Pradesh. HRF accused Gilboa, who was identified as a member of the Israeli military's 271st Combat Engineering Battalion, of involvement in the demolition of civilian buildings in Khan Younis and Rafah.According to reports, HRF submitted material, including geolocated videos, social media posts and chain-of-command documentation to Indian authorities. Gilboa was subsequently traced by pro-Palestinian activists to locations including Old Manali and Gondla in Himachal Pradesh before leaving India.The latest case has followed a similar sequence, with HRF identifying an Israeli soldier through publicly available information, filing a complaint with Indian authorities and the individual subsequently leaving the country.India has long been a popular destination for young Israelis after their mandatory military service. Many undertake an extended post-service trip, commonly known as "tiul gadol", which can last several months.The trend has also contributed to the informal "Hummus Trail" followed by Israeli travellers across several Indian destinations, including Kasol, Dharamkot, Goa, Hampi, Gokarna, Kodaikanal, Rishikesh, Varanasi and Pushkar.Tourism has also featured in India-Israel bilateral cooperation. In February 2026, Israel allocated 4 million shekels for initiatives aimed at strengthening tourism ties with India.The HRF has increasingly sought to pursue legal complaints against Israeli military personnel over alleged conduct during Israel's military campaign in Gaza. The organisation's complaints have also brought attention to the presence of former and serving Israeli military personnel travelling in countries including India.Israel launched its military campaign in Gaza following the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.
Article Summary: Second israeli soldier to leave india after complaint by palestinian rights group. The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left india in mid-september. It remains unclear whether the complaint influenced his departure or whether he left after completing his holiday.

Article Title: 'Unwarranted': India rejects OIC's Kashmir references, slams outfit for giving platform to Pakistan
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) over references to Jammu and Kashmir in a joint communique of its Contact Group, calling them “unwarranted and factually incorrect” and asserting that the grouping has no locus standi to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India.The ministry of external affairs said the entire Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are an “integral and inalienable part of India”, adding that “no amount of repetition of politically motivated propaganda can change this reality”.The response came after Pakistan’s foreign ministry said on X that deputy prime minister and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar had addressed a ministerial meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.According to Pakistan, Dar urged OIC member states to maintain a “unified position” on Jammu and Kashmir at the United Nations and other international fora. He also reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to a “just and peaceful settlement of the dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people”.The references to Jammu and Kashmir drew a strong response from New Delhi.“India categorically rejects the unwarranted and factually incorrect references to India in the Joint Communique of the so-called OIC Contact Group on Jammu & Kashmir. The OIC has no locus standi to pronounce on matters that are strictly internal to India,” the MEA said in a statement.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal shared the statement on X, reiterating India’s position on the OIC communique.The ministry also questioned the credibility of the grouping over its repeated backing of what it described as politically motivated narratives.“Repeated endorsement of such motivated narratives only raises serious questions on the credibility of OIC,” the MEA said.India further turned its focus on Pakistan, saying the OIC should address terrorism emanating from Pakistani territory instead of providing Islamabad a platform for what New Delhi called “fabricated and motivated propaganda”.“Instead of offering a platform to Pakistan to peddle its fabricated and motivated propaganda, OIC will be better advised to counsel Pakistan, which has a well-documented record of supporting and sponsoring terrorism, to look inwards and address the continuing threat of terrorism emanating from territories under its control,” the MEA said.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday delivered a split verdict on whether the challenge to the law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners should be considered by a Constitution Bench.Under the law, the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, a Union cabinet minister and the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.Justice Dipankar Datta countered the Centre's argument against the collegium system for appointing judges, saying the perception that "judges appoint judges" is a myth.Justice Datta also said that there was no need to refer the case to the constitution bench and a two-judge bench can examine its validity.Last month, underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners, Supreme Court said Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. Article Title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that the fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. Though Sastri never publicly spoke about it, it is widely believed that the new arrangement was perceived by him as a dilution in power. By January 1990, the appointment of the two commissioners was rescinded and the EC reverted to being a single—member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with the appointment of election commissioners M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. Seshan viewed the appointments as a direct assault on the independence of his office and completely refused to recognize the two new commissioners. He refused to share official documents with Gill and Krishnamurthy, barred them from attending critical meetings, and would not allocate them any office work. He openly ridiculed the election commissioners in interviews, even referring to them as “two donkeys in my office”.Interestingly, it was on Seshan’s plea challenging the govt’s decision to make EC a multi-member body that the Supreme Court had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power and decision-making authority and that the CEC was only “first among equals”.The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down upon the end of his tenure, Gopalaswami wrote to the President of India recommending the removal of Chawla on grounds of a pro-Congress bias. In his note to the President, Gopalaswami alleged that Chawla was passing on details of EC’s meetings to senior Congress leaders, often taking “toilet breaks” during commission meetings to do so. Gopalaswami’s recommendation was however turned down by the Manmohan Singh govt and Chawla succeeded him as CEC.During the 2019 general election, the differences between then CEC Sunil Arora and then election commissioner Ashok Lavasa came to the fore, with media reports alleging that he had dissented in cases relating to complaints of alleged model code of conduct violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah, but was overruled without the commission making his dissent noted public. EC put out a clarification that dissent notes were only made public in quasi-judicial orders passed by EC.Lavasa resigned on August 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure, and joined the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank (ADB) as its Vice-President.Arun Goyal was the last election commissioner to quit in the middle of his term. Though he had cited personal reasons in his resignation dated March 9, 2024, it was widely speculated that he was not on the best of terms with the then chief election commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
Article Summary: The fault lines within the election commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989. During the 2019 general election, the differences between then cec sunil arora and then election commissioner ashok lavasa came to the fore.

Article Title: LoP's presence in panel to pick CEC, ECs 'ornamental': SC judge
Article Text:
It would not be a fallacious metaphor if it is said that since the umpire is picked by the captain of one side ... and his team wins, even if the decisions taken by such umpire are correct, it has the patina of suspicion: Justice Dipankar Datta

NEW DELHI: Deliberating on the validity of the law on appointment of chief election commissioner and election commissioners by a panel of the PM, a cabinet minister and the leader of opposition, Justice Dipankar Datta on Wednesday pointed out drawbacks and said it gave "overwhelming" power to the executive and made the presence of the LoP "ornamental", undermining the appearance of independence in the selection process. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body."Over seven decades, every dispensation wresting office found it convenient to keep institutions which the Constitution envisioned to be independent under their control. To enact a law on the lines empowered by Article 324(2) would have meant freeing the ECI from exclusive executive control and inviting trouble for the ruling regime. To the mind of this court, this has not been the failing of any one party or one period. A consistent trait of political power, discernible over the decades, has been to preserve leverage over the very body that is meant to judge its claim to power," Justice Datta said.He said if free and fair elections were to be ensured, it was axiomatic that the EC must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently and it was "painful to note that not a single party in power, entrusted by the people of India to govern this great nation", took the initiative of enacting a law of the nature which Article 324(2) left to the supreme law-making body, ie Parliament, to legislate.Also read: SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning "Placing its own electoral fortunes in the hands of a truly independent arbiter was not favoured by any political party, for obvious reasons. To remain in power, the consistent pursuit through executive action has indeed been simple - influence the composition of the EC, control the process of appointment of CEC and ECs and, thereby, temper adverse electoral outcomes," Justice Datta said.Summarising the contentions raised against the law, he added, "The bottom line of the argument runs thus: it would not be a fallacious metaphor if it is said that since the umpire is picked by the captain of one side in a cricket match and his team wins, even if the decisions taken by such umpire are correct, it has the patina of suspicion, for, at the end of the day, the umpire has effectively been chosen by the winning captain. "Justice Datta further said, "There can be no gainsaying that free and fair elections, to a large extent, depend on a truly independent EC. It is not enough for the EC to be independent, it must also appear to be independent. The minister nominated by the prime minister, to function as the third member on the selection committee chaired by the prime minister, cannot be expected to defy his own nominator. In such a circumstance, the inclusion of a minister in the selection committee fails to provide the independent counterweight that a neutral selector could and he would merely echo the voice of his leader; and, consequently, the presence of the leader of opposition in the selection committee becomes largely ornamental, without furthering the purpose of his inclusion. "
Article Summary: Justice dipankar datta said it gave "overwhelming" power to the executive. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body. To enact a law on the lines empowered by article 324(2) would have meant freeing the eci from exclusive executive control, he said.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday questioned the functioning of the Election Commission, saying governments formed during a period when the poll panel was not acting impartially were “unconstitutional”.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Yadav referred to a report that said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and electoral roll procedures.Yadav said the Election Commission was regarded as an impartial institution and was expected to strengthen democracy. Would the Election Commission have been fair? Would it have been impartial?” he asked.Yadav said the reported objections from within the poll panel raised questions about the functioning of an institution whose basic expectation was impartiality.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” he said, alleging that democracy had been “trampled upon”.In an earlier post on X, Yadav described the reported objections by the two Election Commissioners as “extremely serious news”.“It is extremely serious news that in the last 10 months, two Election Commissioners have recorded their objections 14 times to the wrong decisions of the Election Commission,” he said.“Making democracy a victim by becoming puppets of some people in power is a grave constitutional crime.
